# pve_vms (Data Source)

Lists the virtual machines on one Proxmox VE node as reported by `GET /nodes/{node}/qemu`. Configuration options not modeled by this provider (disk, memory, network settings, and so on) are never sent to the API by this data source and remain untouched.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# List every virtual machine on node pve1.

data "pve_vms" "pve1" {
  node = "pve1"
}

output "running_vmids" {
  value = [for vm in data.pve_vms.pve1.vms : vm.vmid if vm.status == "running"]
}

# Request the full status field set (qmpstatus, running_qemu, pressure
# gauges, and so on) for running VMs.

data "pve_vms" "pve1_full" {
  node = "pve1"
  full = true
}

output "qmp_states" {
  value = { for vm in data.pve_vms.pve1_full.vms : vm.vmid => vm.qmpstatus }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node` (String) The cluster node name whose virtual machines to list.

### Optional

- `full` (Boolean) Request the full status of running VMs. Per the API, `full=1` adds the fields `memhost`, `pid`, `qmpstatus`, `running_machine`, `running_qemu`, and the `pressure*` gauges for active VMs; those fields are empty without it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The node name, mirroring the `node` attribute.
- `vms` (Attributes List) Virtual machines on the node, ordered as returned by the API. Fields that PVE omits for a given VM are empty. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vms))

<a id="nestedatt--vms"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vms`

Read-Only:

- `cpu` (Number) Current CPU usage.
- `cpus` (Number) Maximum usable CPUs.
- `diskread` (Number) Bytes the guest read from its block devices since start (not available for all storage types).
- `diskwrite` (Number) Bytes the guest wrote to its block devices since start (not available for all storage types).
- `lock` (String) The current config lock, if any.
- `maxdisk` (Number) Root disk size in bytes.
- `maxmem` (Number) Maximum memory in bytes.
- `mem` (Number) Currently used memory in bytes, from ballooning when available; does not include KSM effects.
- `memhost` (Number) Current memory usage on the host, in bytes (requires `full`).
- `name` (String) VM (host)name.
- `netin` (Number) Traffic in bytes sent to the guest over the network since start.
- `netout` (Number) Traffic in bytes sent from the guest over the network since start.
- `pid` (Number) PID of the QEMU process, if the VM is running (requires `full`).
- `pressurecpufull` (Number) CPU Full pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `pressurecpusome` (Number) CPU Some pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `pressureiofull` (Number) IO Full pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `pressureiosome` (Number) IO Some pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `pressurememoryfull` (Number) Memory Full pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `pressurememorysome` (Number) Memory Some pressure stall average over the last 10 seconds (requires `full`).
- `qmpstatus` (String) VM run state from the `query-status` QMP monitor command (requires `full`).
- `running_machine` (String) The currently running machine type, if running (requires `full`).
- `running_qemu` (String) The QEMU version the VM is currently using, if running (requires `full`).
- `serial` (Boolean) Whether the guest has a serial device configured.
- `status` (String) QEMU process status. Must be one of: `stopped`, `running`.
- `tags` (String) The currently configured tags, if any.
- `template` (Boolean) Whether the guest is a template.
- `uptime` (Number) Uptime in seconds.
- `vmid` (Number) The unique VM ID (100 to 999999999).
